title: After Pentagon Official Took Office, His Family Firm’s Clients Won Up to $3.5 Billion in Military Contracts
author: Peter Castagno

media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F328b87a7-e92d-4996-8e6d-65142c3218e1_2400x1800.jpeg)An
undated portrait of Michael Dodd, assistant secretary of war for critical
technologies. Photo by the War Department.

A senior War Department official who pledged to sell his stake in his family's
defense consulting firm still owns between $1 million and $5 million in the
company over a year after his confirmation, according to his financial
disclosures.

The official, Michael Dodd, is the assistant secretary of war for critical
technologies. His office writes the Pentagon's technology roadmaps, which lay
out what technologies the military needs as well as plans and funding
strategies to develop them. In a September 2026
[interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=azGUuWMdBng), he said these
responsibilities give him "significant influence on what the services
procure."

The firm he founded, Dioltas, [helps companies](https://www.dioltas.com/about)
move "critical technology" through the Pentagon contracting process, "from
first relationship to strategic partnership to funding." Dodd's wife, Melanie,
was the registered agent and treasurer for Dioltas until November, and their
son Keegan is its manager, according to government filings. The three of them
are listed as the owners of Dioltas's office in Indiana, according to property
records. (Their other son, Carson, works as a business analyst at the firm.)

Companies listed as Dioltas clients, according to his 2025 nominee
[disclosure](https://projects.propublica.org/trump-team-financial-
disclosures/appointees/dodd-michael/) report, have won Pentagon contracts or
other funding worth up to $4.3 billion since September 2025, more than $100
million of it already committed. Most of that money, up to about $3.5 billion
of it, was awarded to Dioltas's clients in contracts that the Pentagon
solicited after Dodd was confirmed by the Senate that month. These clients
include defense-technology firms ManTech International and JRC Integrated
Systems, counter-drone company Allen Control Systems, and the microelectronics
manufacturer SkyWater Technology. Drop Site News asked the firms if they were
current clients of Dioltas, and whether Dioltas helped them win the Pentagon
contracts awarded after Dodd's confirmation. None of the firms responded. Dodd
himself did not respond to requests for comment.

The full list of Dioltas's current clients is not public.

Dodd is one of many federal
[officials](https://www.propublica.org/article/george-kollitides-pentagon-
contracts-alvarez-marsal) with ties to [venture
capital](https://thebulletin.org/2026/07/the-rise-of-the-military-technology-
complex/) and [private equity](https://prospect.org/2026/10/16/pentagon-
buyout-king-stephen-feinberg/) who have assumed [senior Pentagon
posts](https://www.thenation.com/article/world/silicon-valley-private-equity-
pentagon-war-profiteering-military-tech-vc/) in the second Trump
administration, as the department steers billions of dollars to new tech firms
through fast-tracked contracts, often with limited oversight.

Dodd's apparent conflicts of interest are not exceptional. They reflect
business as usual under President Donald Trump. From the
[president](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/crypto/trumps-1-4-billion-haul-
makes-him-biggest-us-crypto-moneymaker) on down, administration officials have
regularly engaged in various forms of self-dealing. President Trump's second
term is unique, according to many ethics experts, in its numerous officials'
disregard for the separation between public duties and private interests.

Dodd worked as an advisor to "several prominent" venture capital funds with
defense portfolios, according to his [official
biography](https://www.war.gov/About/Biographies/Biography/Article/4317638/michael-
mike-dodd/), and shepherded their companies through the Pentagon's acquisition
process. He listed 8VC, a [top defense tech
investor](https://readsludge.com/2026/08/31/lonsdale-nonprofit-lobbies-on-
defense-policy-tied-to-his-investments/), as his sole business relationship
aside from Dioltas in his 2025 Senate Armed Services Committee questionnaire.
His [resume](https://www.cake.me/resumes/michael-dodd) shows that he began
advising the firm in November 2024, but this work is not listed on his 2025
ethics disclosure. It is unclear when Dodd stopped advising 8VC.

Between November 2024 and Dodd's March 2025 nomination, 8VC portfolio firms
received at least $100 million through deals with the Defense Innovation Unit,
a Pentagon initiative with headquarters in Silicon Valley. The unit focuses on
forging closer ties between the military and tech industry. At the same time
that Dodd was advising 8VC, he held a senior position at the Defense
Innovation Unit, where he developed its investment strategy and helped manage
funding projects with defense-tech startups, according to his [official
biography](https://www.war.gov/About/Biographies/Biography/Article/4317638/michael-
mike-dodd/). The Defense Innovation Unit did not respond to Drop Site's
questions about Dodd's role with 8VC.

8VC's founder and managing partner is Joe Lonsdale, a Palantir co-founder who
is now helping shape the Pentagon's future tech priorities as a
[participant](https://www.mitre.org/news-insights/publication/project-
meridian) in Project Meridian, a [controversial new
initiative](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/mike-rogers-senate-michigan-iran-
war-hegseth) that enlists defense-tech investors to advise the future of U.S.
warfare. 8VC is a top investor in autonomous military tech firms Anduril--
whose founder Palmer Luckey is Meridian's co-director--and Saronic, whose CEO
Dino Mavrookas and [strategic advisor](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/were-
proud-to-welcome-general-james-e-rainey-share-7459689663977533440-f-hs/) Gen.
James Rainey are also Meridian panelists. Lonsdale has
[argued](https://blog.joelonsdale.com/p/america-needs-better-defense-
acquisition) that new defense tech firms "need allies in government," and a
nonprofit he controls has
[lobbied](https://readsludge.com/2026/08/31/lonsdale-nonprofit-lobbies-on-
defense-policy-tied-to-his-investments/) the Pentagon on defense contracting
reform.

8VC's portfolio firms have done business in Dodd's [technology
areas](https://www.war.gov/About/Biographies/Biography/Article/4317638/michael-
mike-dodd/). For example, Lonsdale co-founded Epirus, a defense contractor
that creates directed-energy systems which has received around $30 million
since Dodd took office. In September, Dodd said he would "[knuckle
roll](https://defensescoop.com/2026/09/10/joint-laser-weapon-system-program-
military-services-critical-tech/)" military services to accelerate adoption of
directed-energy technology.

8VC did not respond to Drop Site's questions about Dodd's involvement with the
firm.

The Pentagon also did not answer Drop Site's questions about Dodd's
relationship with Dioltas and other clients. A spokesperson for the War
Department said, "The Department of War maintains a rigorous, multi-layered
ethics framework that includes financial disclosure reviews, divestitures
where appropriate, and screening to prevent conflicts of interest. Every DOW
official, including Hon. Mike Dodd, is in full compliance with all ethical
laws and regulations. Any claims otherwise are false."

Dioltas, in a response to an inquiry, said only, "We highly encourage you to
check the facts."

## "At the Speed of Business"

In his May 2025 [ethics
agreement](https://extapps2.oge.gov/201/Presiden.nsf/PAS+Index/503C819D84EAA43F85258C9E002CA293/$FILE/Dodd%2C%20Michael%20%20finalEA.pdf),
Dodd pledged to resign from Dioltas "upon confirmation" and said that within
90 days of assuming his role at the Pentagon, he would divest his ownership in
the company by selling his stake. He also said that his wife's role with the
firm "will also end when my interest is sold." Those pledges do not appear to
have been upheld.

The Senate confirmed Dodd on September 18, 2025. But he did not resign from
Dioltas until September 2026, according to Indiana Secretary of State
[records](https://inbiz.in.gov/business-search/details/202109011519549). On
the same day that he resigned from Dioltas, the records show, his wife took
over as the firm's registered agent and his son Keegan became its manager. Two
days after telling Drop Site to "check the facts," Dodd's son replaced his
wife as registered agent, according to a federal disclosure filed on November
17.

Dodd still owns between $1 million and $5 million in Dioltas, according to his
most recent annual financial disclosure, which he signed in May and which a
government ethics lawyer formally approved in September. That disclosure also
shows that, throughout 2025, he received $170,000 from Dioltas.

"There's a general prohibition on using public office for private gain,"
Virginia Canter, a former government ethics lawyer, told Drop Site. "I don't
understand why DoD would allow him, as a Pentagon official, to retain a
financial interest in a company whose business involves facilitating
relationships between the Pentagon and its clients. It just seems like an
obvious conflict of interest if he or his family members continue to profit
from that business."

While Dodd advised defense startups on how to navigate the Pentagon, he
simultaneously held senior government positions at the Defense Innovation
Unit, or DIU. Dodd worked for DIU from at least 2022 until September 2025,
when he was confirmed as assistant secretary of critical technologies, a
position that helps steer the military's defense-industrial policy. The six
defense-tech sectors that Dioltas [works](https://www.dioltas.com/who-we-
serve) in, including quantum technologies and microelectronics, overlap with
sectors that Dodd's Pentagon office manages. If a contractor's work falls
outside those sectors, Dioltas [advertises](https://www.dioltas.com/who-we-
serve) the ability to introduce it to "stakeholders defining future needs."

"The people who shape requirements and fund programs know us by name because
we work alongside them," Dioltas's [website](https://www.dioltas.com/who-we-
serve) boasts, one of at least a dozen references on the site to its ability
to connect clients with government officials to help them earn contracts.
Dioltas says it will stay "behind the scenes, where the work gets done" as it
guides clients "through the moments where access means something."

Since Dodd's confirmation, Dioltas has made at least a dozen social-media
posts promoting his official appearances at industry conferences that Dioltas
also attended. It has described these events as
[opportunities](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ndia-emergingtechnology-
defenseinnovation-
share-7501012187382095872-H0Z6/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAACm2f20BphRiXTPJoz2Hxq3la3GEJVTHafo)
to [engage](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/fedsupernova-defenseinnovation-
defensetech-
ugcPost-7497658473640529920-mISj/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAACm2f20BphRiXTPJoz2Hxq3la3GEJVTHafo)
with government leaders, and in one case it urged its followers to register
for an event [hosted](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/register-below-for-
critical-technologies-
ugcPost-7514394829448019968-pwfr/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAACm2f20BphRiXTPJoz2Hxq3la3GEJVTHafo)
by Dodd's Pentagon office. The event, held in October, introduced the
successor to a research contract managed by the Defense Technical Information
Center, which reports to Dodd's office. Under the current version of the
contract, ManTech, which Dioltas has previously listed as a client, won two
awards worth up to around $542 million earlier this year. DTIC did not answer
Drop Site's questions about whether Dodd's office was involved.

Wes Bryant, an Air Force special operations veteran who served as chief of the
Pentagon's recently [shuttered](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/minab-school-
massacre-iran-war-children-families) Civilian Protection Center, told Drop
Site that Dioltas was "very clearly, without saying it, selling access
directly to him right on their website."

Bryant previously worked in business development for defense contractors
including L3Harris. A key objective of the work was developing relationships
with Pentagon officials. He said that he was required to log each government
contact he engaged and rate their value for influencing contract decisions.

Someone in Dodd's position would be deemed high value. "Those are the
relationships that people out in industry salivate over," Bryant said.

Dodd has championed acquisition reform as a primary [means](https://www.armed-
services.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/dodd_aqp_responses.pdf) of accelerating the
military's adoption of commercial technology. He has advocated the expansion
of a [controversial](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/the-pentagon-has-
gone-too-far-in-using-the-other-transaction-authority-congress-should-act/)
funding arrangement that fast-tracks the contracting process and
[sidesteps](https://www.pogo.org/reports/other-transactions-do-the-rewards-
outweigh-the-risks) federal acquisition regulations, known as "Other
Transaction Authority" (OTA). As assistant secretary for critical
technologies, Dodd works within the Office of Research and Engineering, which
supervises department-wide prototyping of technology, much of which runs
through OTAs.

"If I meet a non-traditional company that I'm interested in, I can get them on
contract at the speed of business," Dodd said in an October
[interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DPtrCPCn8Mc).

William Hartung, an expert on Pentagon budgeting, described OTAs as lucrative
long-term commitments with minimal oversight. "Dodd's promotion of OTAs could
pad the bottom lines of Dioltas's clients," he told Drop Site.

Companies with ties to Dodd have received fast-tracked funding in technology
areas he oversees. For example, SkyWater Technology, a Dioltas client and
microelectronics manufacturer, received $30.9 million in OTA funding in June.
Dodd gave a speech at a [SkyWater-hosted
event](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/hon-mike-dodd-
aa70a11_america250-microelectronics-americaningenuity-
ugcPost-7485731373161418752-6w6Z/) the following month and invests up to
$15,000 in the firm, according to his disclosures. Allen Control Systems, a
startup with no federal contracts in procurement records before Dodd took
office, received two prototype OTAs worth at least $6.5 million earlier this
year, which funded efforts to adapt its technology for the Army and the
Marines. It then won an Army counter-drone contract [worth
up](https://www.bizjournals.com/austin/news/2026/10/01/anti-drone-startup-
wins-army-contract-texas.html) to $500 million in September, and a few months
later, in mid-November, it was selected to join a [Pentagon directed-
energy](https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/4648762/department-
of-war-invites-seven-industry-teams-to-participate-in-phase-ii-direc/) test
program [designed](https://www.businessinsider.com/pentagon-holding-laser-
weapon-shoot-off-against-drone-targets-2026-11) to lead directly to funding.
Dodd's office is a partner on this program.

Venture capitalists and contractors have pushed to expand the use of OTAs, as
they[ give companies more leverage](https://www.pogo.org/reports/other-
transactions-do-the-rewards-outweigh-the-risks) over negotiations and reduce
transparency and oversight. The Silicon Valley Defense Group celebrated the
Trump administration's embrace of OTAs in its[ 2026 annual
report](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6824e488de9281397c0dfb01/t/6a14a90aae1f4367c7d9c89b/1779738890973/2026+NatSec100+Report-
WEB.pdf)--which included Dodd's statement to investors and founders that "the
Department's checkbook is open" for fast-moving firms.

In recent [interviews](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TSzfR0A5y-w), Dodd has
explained that one way he gets firms on contract as fast as possible is by
routing them through consortiums, or groups of companies. "That can be
literally like same day stuff if we want to get a performer on contract," he
told [Federal News Network](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=azGUuWMdBng) last
month.

Around half of the Pentagon's [OTA
spending](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/the-pentagon-has-gone-too-far-
in-using-the-other-transaction-authority-congress-should-act/) is directed to
consortiums. Federal records list the consortium as the recipient of a federal
contract, and often do not show which individual firms were paid through it.
The Government Accountability Office and the War Department's [Inspector
General](https://www.dodig.mil/reports.html/Article/2582944/audit-of-other-
transactions-awarded-through-consortiums-dodig-2021-077/) have
[repeatedly](https://www.nationaldefensemagazine.org/articles/2025/9/19/pentagon-
lacks-ability-to-track-other-transaction-agreements-gao-finds) flagged weak
oversight of these middlemen.

## "A Conflict on Steroids"

Dodd worked as an advisor to the National Security Technology Accelerator, or
NSTXL, from August 2021 to June 2025. NSTXL is a nonprofit that manages
consortia of defense companies and handles
[billions](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2020/12/30/space-force-
contract/) in Pentagon contracts, including a Space Force OTA worth up to
[$12.1
billion](https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/award/view/FA88142190001?agencyID=9700&modNumber=P00166&transactionNumber=0&refIdvPiid=null&idvAgencyID=null&contractType=AWARD).
NSTXL [now
manages](https://x.com/ASWCTDoddFather/status/2095620504631513244?a=frjQio3ArvaBGM2xwig&s=20)
OTA contracts for Dodd's[ department](https://nstxl.org/opportunity/decuas/),
including a new[ ](https://insidedefense.com/insider/nstxl-tapped-
lead-500m-pentagon-directed-energy-consortium)OTA related to energy weapons
worth up to [$500 million](https://insidedefense.com/insider/nstxl-tapped-
lead-500m-pentagon-directed-energy-consortium).

Another OTA it manages, which is used across the Pentagon's research and
engineering office, has handled more than $3 billion in awards, according to
[NSTXL](https://nstxl.org/3b-and-counting-s2marts-otas-impact-on-defense-
technology/). Dodd's Pentagon microelectronics program, the Microelectronics
Commons, is among the projects that run through it. Dodd
[delivered](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsVeLks8YL8&t=11s) the Pentagon's
leadership keynote at the Microelectronics Commons annual meeting in February,
an event organized by NSTXL, where Dioltas said it [spent the
week](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/commonsannual-nationalsecurity-
supplychain-
ugcPost-7430653585719447552-JHxn/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAACm2f20BphRiXTPJoz2Hxq3la3GEJVTHafo)
"engaging with our portfolio companies, industry partners, and Department of
War leadership."

Drop Site reviewed more than $100 million worth of recent OTAs to NSTXL that
do not detail which member firms were paid. NSTXL does not list its members
publicly, and according to its [tax
filings](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/825338732),
it has no written policy for document retention, whistleblowers, and conflicts
of interest.

NSTXL reported over $10 million in losses in its two most recent tax filings
for
[2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/825338732/202413209349311101/full)
and
[2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/825338732/202523219349303587/full).
Over the same period, it transferred over $10 million more than its entire
revenue to a for-profit firm owned by its founder.

NSTXL reported $66.9 million in revenue over 2023 and 2024--mostly from
government fees--but paid its contract consultant Innovas a total of $77.3
million over the same period. Tim Greeff, the founder and president of NSTXL,
is also CEO and majority owner of Innovas, according to the filings.

Dodd reported $303,000 in income and bonus fees from Innovas in both of his
disclosures.

NSTXL and Innovas did not respond to Drop Site's inquiries.

Hartung called NSTXL's relationship with Dodd "a conflict on steroids," adding
that "Congress should force disclosure of companies NSTXL funnels money to and
look more closely at Dodd's role in brokering and possibly profiting from
these arrangements."
